children: A jump in corporate tax receipts last month pushed Ireland's year-to-date tax take up 10.7% when one-off proceeds of Apple
back taxes are excluded, the finance ministry said on Friday.

A surge in corporate tax, mainly paid by a small number of US multinationals, has helped drive Ireland's overall revenues to record levels and the treasury collected €4.9 billion from companies in September compared with €1.8 billion a year ago.

Corporate tax receipts for the first nine months of the year rose to €22.7 billion, 24% higher than the same period last year, and accounted for close to one-third of the €78.9 billion in tax revenue collected so far this year.
The data also showed that Ireland's strongly growing economy continues to push up the other two main tax categories, with income tax and VAT receipts up 7.8% and 8.9% respectively so far this year.

The strong growth in government revenue will allow ministers to announce another generous annual budget package of tax cuts and spending increases on Tuesday, a rarity in Europe where many countries' public finances are precariously stretched.

Government spending this year was up 7.7% year-on-year to €83.4 billion by the end of September, the data showed, with expenditure on day-to-day services growing at a faster pace than investment in public infrastructure.
